name: Sudan
summary: Two hundred Nubian pyramids at Meroe and Nuri, the Nile making its great bend through desert, and a Red Sea coast with reefs nobody dives — a country with an extraordinary past and a hard present.
when: November to March, and only when the security situation allows it.

entries.caption: The Pyramids of Meroe
entries.description: Two hundred of them on a ridge of sand, steeper and smaller than Egypt's, and empty.
entries.subject: the Nubian pyramids of Meroe standing on desert dunes

entries.caption: The Great Bend
entries.description: The Nile turns southwest for three hundred kilometres here, against every expectation.
entries.subject: the Nile curving through desert at the great bend in northern Sudan

entries.caption: Dinder and the Red Sea
entries.description: Dinder on the Ethiopian border holds lion, giraffe and roan; the reefs hold everything else.
entries.subject: a herd of roan antelope in Dinder National Park

entries.caption: Dinder
entries.description: One of Africa's oldest national parks, and one of the least visited on the continent.
entries.subject: acacia woodland and a waterhole in Dinder National Park

entries.caption: The Red Sea Hills and Jebel Marra
entries.description: Granite hills behind Port Sudan, and a volcanic crater lake on Jebel Marra in Darfur.
entries.subject: the volcanic crater lake on Jebel Marra

entries.caption: The Cataracts
entries.description: Six of them on the Nile, rapids where the river crosses granite, and boats have to portage.
entries.subject: white water over black granite at a Nile cataract

entries.caption: The Blue and the White
entries.description: They meet at Khartoum, one clear and one brown, and you can see the line between them.
entries.subject: the confluence of the Blue and White Nile at Khartoum from the air

entries.caption: Reefs Nobody Dives
entries.description: Sanganeb atoll and Sha'ab Rumi, where Cousteau sank Conshelf II and the coral grew over it.
entries.subject: a coral wall and reef fish at Sanganeb atoll in the Red Sea

entries.caption: Acacia and Doum Palm
entries.description: Gum arabic comes from the acacia belt across the middle of the country. Most of the world's does.
entries.subject: an acacia woodland tapped for gum arabic in central Sudan

entries.caption: Diving and Desert Driving
entries.description: Liveaboards out of Port Sudan, and four-wheel-drive routes between the pyramid fields.
entries.subject: a dive boat anchored over a reef in the Sudanese Red Sea

entries.caption: Nubian, Arab, Beja
entries.description: Nubian along the northern Nile, Beja in the Red Sea hills, and nearly six hundred groups altogether.
entries.subject: a decorated Nubian house with a painted doorway on the Nile

entries.caption: The Nubians
entries.description: The Nubian villages along the northern Nile paint their houses, and have done for a very long time.
entries.subject: a Nubian woman in a doorway of a brightly painted house

entries.caption: Ful and Kisra
entries.description: Ful medames for breakfast everywhere, kisra sorghum flatbread, and coffee spiced with ginger.
entries.subject: a bowl of ful medames with bread and tea on a table

entries.caption: Sufi Friday at Omdurman
entries.description: The Hamed al-Nil tomb, every Friday at sunset, drumming and whirling for two hours.
entries.subject: Sufi dervishes in green and red at the Hamed al-Nil tomb, Omdurman

entries.caption: Basketry and Silver
entries.description: Coiled palm baskets from the north, Beja swords, and silver from the Omdurman souk.
entries.subject: coiled palm-fibre baskets in bright colours at Omdurman souk

entries.caption: Meroe, Nuri and El-Kurru
entries.description: Three royal cemeteries of the Kingdom of Kush, which ruled Egypt for a century.
entries.subject: the pyramid field at Nuri with the Nile beyond

entries.caption: Kush
entries.description: Gebel Barkal was the holy mountain of two kingdoms, and the temple of Amun is cut into it.
entries.subject: the flat-topped Gebel Barkal with the temple ruins at its base

entries.caption: Khartoum and Omdurman
entries.description: Two cities facing each other across the confluence, one colonial grid and one enormous souk.
entries.subject: the Omdurman souk crowded with people and stalls

entries.caption: Mud Brick and Painted Doors
entries.description: Nubian vaulted mud-brick houses with painted gates, a technique revived by Hassan Fathy.
entries.subject: a vaulted Nubian mud-brick house with a painted gateway

entries.caption: The Camel Market
entries.description: Omdurman's camel market on a Saturday, with animals in from Kordofan and Darfur.
entries.subject: camels and traders at the Omdurman camel market

entries.caption: The Nile at Tuti
entries.description: The island in the confluence, farmed, walkable, and reached by ferry from three sides.
entries.subject: small farms and palms on Tuti island in the Nile at Khartoum

entries.caption: Walking Between Pyramids
entries.description: There is no fence at Meroe. You walk in off the sand and up the ridge.
entries.subject: footprints in sand leading up to the Meroe pyramids

entries.caption: Very Little
entries.description: A handful of Red Sea liveaboards, and camps at Meroe. That is the whole of it.
entries.subject: a tented camp on sand within sight of the Meroe pyramids

entries.caption: Gum Arabic and the Acacia Belt
entries.description: A gum tapped from wild acacia by hand, in most of the soft drinks in the world.
entries.subject: a tapped acacia trunk with gum arabic crystals on the bark

entries.caption: Pyramids and Dunes
entries.description: Meroe an hour after dawn, when the sand is still ridged and the shadows are long.
entries.subject: long shadows across dunes below the Meroe pyramids at dawn

entries.caption: Old Dongola
entries.description: A Christian Nubian capital on the Nile, with a throne hall that became a mosque.
entries.subject: the ruined columns and throne hall of Old Dongola above the Nile

entries.caption: Why Sudan
entries.description: More pyramids than Egypt, no queue at any of them, and a welcome people write books about.
entries.subject: a lone figure walking among the pyramids of Meroe
